8	/-!
9	# THE ℙ¹ TWO-CHART COBOUNDARY SUBGROUP: THE REDUCED CASE, AND THE GENERAL-RING EXPONENT
10	
11	`Picard/LaurentTwoChartCoboundary.lean` characterises the ℙ¹ two-chart coboundary subgroup
12	`laurentCoboundaryUnits A` — a Laurent unit is a coboundary **iff** it is `C c` for a unit `c` —
13	**over a domain**, and records why the forward direction (a coboundary is a constant) needs the
14	domain: `Polynomial.isUnit_iff` sees only constant units of `A[X]`, but at a non-reduced ring
15	`1 + C e · p` with `e² = 0` is a non-constant unit.  `Algebra/LaurentNilpotentCoboundary.lean`
16	then handles the opposite extreme — a unit congruent to `1` modulo a **nilpotent** is a
17	coboundary, over an arbitrary ring — leaving the two remaining pieces named in its header: the
18	**reduced** case, and the general-ring bridge from a degree/exponent-zero condition to the
19	constant-modulo-nilpotent normal form.
20	
21	This file supplies both, **adding no hypothesis to any existing statement** — it weakens
22	`IsDomain` to `IsReduced` (a strict weakening: `k × k` is reduced and not a domain), and it
23	states the general-ring forward structure with no ring hypothesis at all.
24	
25	## 1. Over a reduced ring, a coboundary is a constant unit
26	
27	`Polynomial.isUnit_iff_coeff_isUnit_isNilpotent` classifies units of `A[X]` over *any* commutative
28	ring — unit constant term, nilpotent higher coefficients.  Over a **reduced** ring the nilpotents
29	are `0`, so a polynomial unit is a constant unit, and the exact argument of
30	`eq_C_of_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits` goes through with `IsReduced A` in place of `IsDomain A`.
31	This closes the reduced case: for reduced `A`,
32	
33	```
34	Pic(ℙ¹_A)  =  A[t,t⁻¹]ˣ ⧸ (A[t]ˣ · A[t⁻¹]ˣ)  =  ℤ,
35	```
36	
37	and `t` is the generator (`not_tUnit_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits_reduced`).
38	
39	## 2. Over an arbitrary ring, a coboundary is `C c · (1 + z)` with `z` nilpotent
40	
41	This is the general-ring **exponent-zero** structure.
42	`Polynomial.isUnit_iff_coeff_isUnit_isNilpotent`
43	factors each chart unit as `C cᵢ · (1 + Nᵢ)` with `Nᵢ` nilpotent, and the product of the two chart
44	images is `C (c₀c₁) · (1 + z)` with `z` a nilpotent Laurent element (sum and product of the two
45	nilpotent transported parts).  A coboundary therefore has *no `T`-exponent*: its class in the
46	`ℤ` of the domain computation is `0`, and the deviation from a constant is a nilpotent — exactly
47	the direction a "degree map to `ℤ`" would record, without needing the map (which does not exist
48	over a general ring).  Together with `nilpotent_isUnit_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits`
49	(`LaurentNilpotentCoboundary.lean`, the converse: such a unit *is* a coboundary) this pins the
50	coboundary subgroup at an arbitrary ring as *exactly* `{C c · (1 + z) : c ∈ Aˣ, z nilpotent}`.
51	
52	## Main declarations
53	
54	* `AlgebraicGeometry.polyUnit_eq_C_of_reduced` — a polynomial unit over a reduced ring is a
55	  constant unit.
56	* `AlgebraicGeometry.eq_C_of_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits_reduced` — over a reduced ring, a
57	  coboundary is a constant unit (the forward direction, with `IsDomain` weakened to `IsReduced`).
58	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits_iff_reduced` — the reduced-ring characterisation
59	  as an `iff`.
60	* `AlgebraicGeometry.not_tUnit_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits_reduced` — `t` is not a coboundary over
61	  a nontrivial reduced ring: `Pic(ℙ¹_A) = ℤ` over reduced `A`.
62	* `AlgebraicGeometry.polyUnit_eq_C_mul_one_add_nilpotent` — a polynomial unit over an arbitrary
63	  ring is `C c · (1 + N)`, `c` a unit and `N` nilpotent.
64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.eq_C_mul_one_add_nilpotent_of_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits` — the general-ring
65	  forward structure: a coboundary is `C c · (1 + z)`, `c` a unit and `z` a nilpotent Laurent
66	  element (the exponent-zero normal form).
67	-/
68	
69	set_option autoImplicit false
70	
71	universe u
72	
73	open CategoryTheory
74	
75	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
76	
77	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
78	
79	/-! ## The reduced case: a coboundary is a constant unit -/
80	
81	/-- **A unit of `A[X]` over a reduced ring is a constant unit.**
82	
83	`Polynomial.isUnit_iff_coeff_isUnit_isNilpotent` gives a unit constant term and nilpotent higher
84	coefficients; over a reduced ring the latter are `0`, so `P = C (P.coeff 0)`.  This is the reduced
85	replacement for `Polynomial.isUnit_iff` (which needs `IsDomain`). -/
86	theorem polyUnit_eq_C_of_reduced [_root_.IsReduced A] {P : Polynomial A} (hP : IsUnit P) :
87	    ∃ c : A, IsUnit c ∧ P = Polynomial.C c := by
88	  rw [Polynomial.isUnit_iff_coeff_isUnit_isNilpotent] at hP
89	  obtain ⟨h0, hn⟩ := hP
90	  refine ⟨P.coeff 0, h0, ?_⟩
91	  ext i
92	  rcases eq_or_ne i 0 with rfl | hi
93	  · simp
94	  · simp only [Polynomial.coeff_C, if_neg hi]
95	    exact (hn i hi).eq_zero
96	
97	/-- **Over a reduced ring, a coboundary is a constant unit.**
98	
99	The forward direction of the characterisation, with `IsDomain` weakened to `IsReduced`: both chart
100	unit groups consist of constants (`polyUnit_eq_C_of_reduced`), and both chart maps send
101	`Polynomial.C c` to `LaurentPolynomial.C c`.  This is exactly the argument of
102	`eq_C_of_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits`, run over the strictly larger class of reduced rings. -/
103	theorem eq_C_of_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits_reduced [_root_.IsReduced A]
104	    {u : (LaurentPolynomial A)ˣ} (hu : u ∈ laurentCoboundaryUnits A) :
105	    ∃ c : A, IsUnit c ∧ (u : LaurentPolynomial A) = LaurentPolynomial.C c := by
106	  obtain ⟨v, w, hvw⟩ := TruncExpCech.mem_cechCoboundaryUnits.mp hu
107	  obtain ⟨cv, hcv, hv⟩ := polyUnit_eq_C_of_reduced v.isUnit
108	  obtain ⟨cw, hcw, hw⟩ := polyUnit_eq_C_of_reduced w.isUnit
109	  refine ⟨cv * cw, hcv.mul hcw, ?_⟩
110	  rw [← hvw]
111	  change Polynomial.toLaurent (v : Polynomial A) * (rightChart A) (w : Polynomial A)
112	    = LaurentPolynomial.C (cv * cw)
113	  rw [hv, hw]
114	  simp [rightChart, map_mul]
115	
116	/-- **THE REDUCED-RING CHARACTERISATION**: over a reduced ring the coboundary subgroup is exactly
117	the constants, so the two-chart Čech Picard group of `ℙ¹_A` is `A[t,t⁻¹]ˣ ⧸ Aˣ = ℤ`. -/
118	theorem mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits_iff_reduced [_root_.IsReduced A] {u : (LaurentPolynomial A)ˣ} :
119	    u ∈ laurentCoboundaryUnits A
120	      ↔ ∃ c : A, IsUnit c ∧ (u : LaurentPolynomial A) = LaurentPolynomial.C c := by
121	  refine ⟨eq_C_of_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits_reduced, ?_⟩
122	  rintro ⟨c, hc, hu⟩
123	  obtain ⟨cu, rfl⟩ := hc
124	  have h : u = Units.map (LaurentPolynomial.C : A →+* LaurentPolynomial A).toMonoidHom cu :=
125	    Units.ext hu
126	  rw [h]
127	  exact C_unit_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits cu
128	
129	/-- **`t` IS NOT A COBOUNDARY** over a nontrivial reduced ring — the generator of
130	`Pic(ℙ¹_A) = ℤ`, and the refutation of the universal form of the two-chart criterion, now over
131	the strictly larger class of reduced rings.  Same coefficient comparison as the domain case:
132	if `T 1` were a constant, `exp_unique` would force `1 = 0`. -/
133	theorem not_tUnit_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits_reduced [_root_.IsReduced A] [Nontrivial A] :
134	    LaurentPolynomial.tUnit (R := A) 1 ∉ laurentCoboundaryUnits A := by
135	  intro hmem
136	  obtain ⟨c, _, hc⟩ := eq_C_of_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits_reduced hmem
137	  rw [LaurentPolynomial.tUnit_coe] at hc
138	  have h : (LaurentPolynomial.C (1 : A) * LaurentPolynomial.T (1 : ℤ))
139	      = LaurentPolynomial.C c * LaurentPolynomial.T (0 : ℤ) := by
140	    rw [map_one, one_mul, LaurentPolynomial.T_zero, mul_one]
141	    exact hc
142	  exact absurd (LaurentPolynomial.exp_unique (one_ne_zero (α := A)) h) one_ne_zero
143	
144	/-! ## The general ring: a coboundary has exponent zero (constant times unipotent) -/
145	
146	/-- **A unit of `A[X]` over an arbitrary ring is `C c · (1 + N)`**, `c` a unit and `N` nilpotent.
147	
148	`Polynomial.isUnit_iff_coeff_isUnit_isNilpotent` gives a unit constant term `c = P.coeff 0` and
149	nilpotent higher part `P - C c`; dividing by `C c` leaves `1 + C c⁻¹ · (P - C c)`, and the second
150	summand is nilpotent (a nilpotent times anything, in a commutative ring). -/
151	theorem polyUnit_eq_C_mul_one_add_nilpotent {P : Polynomial A} (hP : IsUnit P) :
152	    ∃ (c : A) (N : Polynomial A), IsUnit c ∧ IsNilpotent N ∧ P = Polynomial.C c * (1 + N) := by
153	  obtain ⟨h0, hn⟩ := (Polynomial.isUnit_iff_coeff_isUnit_isNilpotent).mp hP
154	  obtain ⟨cu, hcu⟩ := h0
155	  have hND : IsNilpotent (P - Polynomial.C (P.coeff 0)) := by
156	    rw [Polynomial.isNilpotent_iff]
157	    intro i
158	    rcases eq_or_ne i 0 with rfl | hi
159	    · simp
160	    · rw [Polynomial.coeff_sub, Polynomial.coeff_C, if_neg hi, sub_zero]
161	      exact hn i hi
162	  refine ⟨P.coeff 0, Polynomial.C (↑cu⁻¹ : A) * (P - Polynomial.C (P.coeff 0)),
163	    ⟨cu, hcu⟩, (Commute.all _ _).isNilpotent_mul_left hND, ?_⟩
164	  have hccu : Polynomial.C (P.coeff 0) * Polynomial.C (↑cu⁻¹ : A) = 1 := by
165	    rw [← Polynomial.C_mul, ← hcu, ← Units.val_mul, mul_inv_cancel, Units.val_one, Polynomial.C_1]
166	  rw [mul_add, mul_one, ← mul_assoc, hccu, one_mul, add_sub_cancel]
167	
168	/-- **THE GENERAL-RING FORWARD STRUCTURE**: over an arbitrary commutative ring a coboundary is
169	`C c · (1 + z)` with `c` a unit and `z` a **nilpotent** Laurent element.
170	
171	Factor each chart unit as `C cᵢ · (1 + Nᵢ)` (`polyUnit_eq_C_mul_one_add_nilpotent`); transporting
172	`Nᵢ` through the two chart maps gives nilpotent Laurent elements `tv, tw`, and the product of the
173	two chart images is `C (cv·cw) · (1 + (tv + tw + tv·tw))`, whose deviation from the constant
174	`C (cv·cw)` is the nilpotent `z = tv + tw + tv·tw`.
175	
176	This is the **exponent-zero** statement in the direction a consumer needs: a coboundary has no
177	`T`-exponent, and its class over the reduction is `1`.  There is no `ℤ`-valued degree map over a
178	general ring to say this with, so it is stated as a normal form; combined with
179	`nilpotent_isUnit_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits` (the converse) it characterises the coboundary
180	subgroup at an arbitrary ring. -/
181	theorem eq_C_mul_one_add_nilpotent_of_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits
182	    {u : (LaurentPolynomial A)ˣ} (hu : u ∈ laurentCoboundaryUnits A) :
183	    ∃ (c : A) (z : LaurentPolynomial A), IsUnit c ∧ IsNilpotent z ∧
184	      (u : LaurentPolynomial A) = LaurentPolynomial.C c * (1 + z) := by
185	  obtain ⟨v, w, hvw⟩ := TruncExpCech.mem_cechCoboundaryUnits.mp hu
186	  obtain ⟨cv, Nv, hcv, hNv, hv⟩ := polyUnit_eq_C_mul_one_add_nilpotent v.isUnit
187	  obtain ⟨cw, Nw, hcw, hNw, hw⟩ := polyUnit_eq_C_mul_one_add_nilpotent w.isUnit
188	  set tv : LaurentPolynomial A := Polynomial.toLaurent Nv with htv
189	  set tw : LaurentPolynomial A := rightChart A Nw with htw
190	  have htvN : IsNilpotent tv :=
191	    hNv.map (Polynomial.toLaurent : Polynomial A →+* LaurentPolynomial A)
192	  have htwN : IsNilpotent tw := hNw.map (rightChart A)
193	  refine ⟨cv * cw, tv + tw + tv * tw, hcv.mul hcw, ?_, ?_⟩
194	  · have h1 : IsNilpotent (tv + tw) := (Commute.all _ _).isNilpotent_add htvN htwN
195	    have h2 : IsNilpotent (tv * tw) := (Commute.all _ _).isNilpotent_mul_left htwN
196	    exact (Commute.all _ _).isNilpotent_add h1 h2
197	  · rw [← hvw]
198	    change Polynomial.toLaurent (v : Polynomial A) * (rightChart A) (w : Polynomial A) = _
199	    rw [hv, hw, map_mul, map_mul, Polynomial.toLaurent_C, rightChart_C,
200	      map_add, map_one, map_add, map_one, ← htv, ← htw, map_mul]
201	    ring
202	
203	end AlgebraicGeometry

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Algebra.LaurentNilpotentCoboundary
7	
8	/-!
9	# NILPOTENCE OF LAURENT POLYNOMIALS IS COEFFICIENTWISE
10	
11	The ℙ¹ two-chart Picard computation over an arbitrary (non-reduced) test ring runs into the
12	nilpotent part of the coefficient ring: over a domain a Laurent unit is `C c · Tⁿ`
13	(`Picard/LaurentTwoChartCoboundary.lean`), over a reduced ring the same
14	(`Algebra/LaurentCoboundaryReduced.lean`), and the gap between reduced and arbitrary is exactly
15	the units congruent to `1` modulo nilpotents.  `Algebra/LaurentReducedReduction.lean` reduces the
16	whole coboundary question to reduced rings; the reduction needs to know that the kernel of
17	`A[T;T⁻¹] → (A ⧸ nil A)[T;T⁻¹]` is the **nilpotent** Laurent polynomials, and that is a
18	coefficientwise statement.
19	
20	This file is that coefficientwise dictionary, and nothing about Picard groups:
21	
22	* `IsReduced (A[T;T⁻¹])` when `A` is reduced — proved by clearing denominators to `A[X]`, where
23	  reducedness is coefficientwise (`Polynomial.isNilpotent_iff`); there is no mathlib instance for
24	  the Laurent ring at this pin;
25	* a coefficient of a nilpotent Laurent polynomial is nilpotent — via base change to the reduced
26	  quotient `A ⧸ nil A`, where the image is `0`;
27	* conversely a Laurent polynomial with all coefficients nilpotent is nilpotent — it is a finite
28	  sum of nilpotent monomials;
29	* a coefficient of a product `x · y` lies in `I · J` when `x`'s coefficients lie in `I` and `y`'s
30	  in `J` — the Cauchy-product membership the halving step of the arbitrary-ring computation needs.
31	
32	## Main declarations
33	
34	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isReduced_laurent` — `A[T;T⁻¹]` is reduced when `A` is.
35	* `AlgebraicGeometry.coeff_isNilpotent_of_isNilpotent` — a coefficient of a nilpotent Laurent
36	  polynomial is nilpotent.
37	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isNilpotent_of_forall_coeff` — a Laurent polynomial with all coefficients
38	  nilpotent is nilpotent.
39	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isNilpotent_laurent_iff_forall_coeff` — the two together, as an `iff`.
40	* `AlgebraicGeometry.coeff_mul_mem_mul` — the Cauchy-product coefficient of `x · y` lies in
41	  `I · J`.
42	-/
43	
44	set_option autoImplicit false
45	
46	universe u
47	
48	open CategoryTheory LaurentPolynomial
49	
50	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
51	
52	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
53	
54	/-- **`A[T;T⁻¹]` is reduced when `A` is.**
55	
56	Clear denominators: any Laurent polynomial `z` is `Polynomial.toLaurent p · T (-a)` for some `p`
57	and `a` (`exists_T_pow`), and multiplying a nilpotent by the unit `T a` keeps it nilpotent, so
58	`toLaurent p` is nilpotent; `toLaurent` is injective, `A[X]` is reduced coefficientwise, so
59	`p = 0` and hence `z = 0`.  Mathlib has no `IsReduced` instance for the Laurent ring at this pin,
60	so it is proved here. -/
61	theorem isReduced_laurent [_root_.IsReduced A] : _root_.IsReduced (LaurentPolynomial A) := by
62	  have hpoly : _root_.IsReduced (Polynomial A) := by
63	    refine ⟨fun p hp => ?_⟩
64	    rw [Polynomial.isNilpotent_iff] at hp
65	    ext i; simpa using (hp i).eq_zero
66	  refine ⟨fun z hz => ?_⟩
67	  obtain ⟨a, p, hp⟩ := LaurentPolynomial.exists_T_pow z
68	  have hpn : IsNilpotent (Polynomial.toLaurent p) := by
69	    rw [hp]; exact (Commute.all _ _).isNilpotent_mul_right hz
70	  have hp0 : p = 0 := by
71	    obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := hpn
72	    have hpp : IsNilpotent p :=
73	      ⟨n, Polynomial.toLaurent_injective (by rw [map_pow, hn, map_zero])⟩
74	    exact hpp.eq_zero
75	  rw [hp0, map_zero] at hp
76	  exact (isUnit_T a).mul_left_eq_zero.mp hp.symm
77	
78	/-- **A coefficient of a nilpotent Laurent polynomial is nilpotent.**
79	
80	Base change to the reduced quotient `A ⧸ nil A`: the image of a nilpotent is nilpotent, and the
81	Laurent ring over a reduced ring is reduced (`isReduced_laurent`), so the image is `0`; reading
82	off coefficient `i` puts `z i` in the nilradical. -/
83	theorem coeff_isNilpotent_of_isNilpotent {z : LaurentPolynomial A} (hz : IsNilpotent z) (i : ℤ) :
84	    IsNilpotent (z i) := by
85	  haveI hrad : (nilradical A).IsRadical := Ideal.radical_isRadical 0
86	  haveI hred : _root_.IsReduced (A ⧸ nilradical A) :=
87	    (Ideal.isRadical_iff_quotient_reduced _).mp hrad
88	  haveI : _root_.IsReduced (LaurentPolynomial (A ⧸ nilradical A)) := isReduced_laurent
89	  have h2 : (AddMonoidAlgebra.mapRingHom ℤ (Ideal.Quotient.mk (nilradical A))) z = 0 :=
90	    (hz.map _).eq_zero
91	  have h3 : Ideal.Quotient.mk (nilradical A) (z i) = 0 := by
92	    have hc := congrArg (fun w : LaurentPolynomial (A ⧸ nilradical A) => w i) h2
93	    rw [AddMonoidAlgebra.mapRingHom_apply] at hc
94	    rw [hc]; rfl
95	  rw [← mem_nilradical]
96	  exact (Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem).mp h3
97	
98	/-- **A Laurent polynomial with all coefficients nilpotent is nilpotent.**
99	
100	It is the finite sum `∑ᵢ C (z i) · T i` over its support, and each summand is nilpotent
101	(`C (z i)` is nilpotent, `T i` a unit). -/
102	theorem isNilpotent_of_forall_coeff {z : LaurentPolynomial A}
103	    (hz : ∀ i, IsNilpotent (z i)) : IsNilpotent z := by
104	  classical
105	  have hrep : z = ∑ i ∈ z.support, (LaurentPolynomial.C (z i) * LaurentPolynomial.T i) := by
106	    conv_lhs => rw [← Finsupp.sum_single z]
107	    rw [Finsupp.sum]
108	    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun i _ => by rw [← LaurentPolynomial.single_eq_C_mul_T])
109	  rw [hrep]
110	  exact isNilpotent_sum fun i _ =>
111	    (Commute.all _ _).isNilpotent_mul_right
112	      ((hz i).map (LaurentPolynomial.C : A →+* LaurentPolynomial A))
113	
114	/-- The two directions together: a Laurent polynomial is nilpotent iff every coefficient is. -/
115	theorem isNilpotent_laurent_iff_forall_coeff {z : LaurentPolynomial A} :
116	    IsNilpotent z ↔ ∀ i, IsNilpotent (z i) :=
117	  ⟨fun hz => coeff_isNilpotent_of_isNilpotent hz, isNilpotent_of_forall_coeff⟩
118	
119	/-- **The Cauchy-product coefficient lies in the product ideal.**  If every coefficient of `x`
120	lies in `I` and every coefficient of `y` in `J`, then every coefficient of `x · y` lies in
121	`I · J`.  This is the membership the halving step of the arbitrary-ring ℙ¹ computation needs:
122	the cross term of two deformations along an ideal `I` lands in `I²`. -/
123	theorem coeff_mul_mem_mul {I J : Ideal A} {x y : LaurentPolynomial A}
124	    (hx : ∀ i, x i ∈ I) (hy : ∀ i, y i ∈ J) (m : ℤ) : (x * y) m ∈ I * J := by
125	  classical
126	  rw [AddMonoidAlgebra.mul_apply, Finsupp.sum]
127	  refine Ideal.sum_mem _ (fun a₁ _ => ?_)
128	  rw [Finsupp.sum]
129	  refine Ideal.sum_mem _ (fun a₂ _ => ?_)
130	  split
131	  · exact Ideal.mul_mem_mul (hx a₁) (hy a₂)
132	  · exact Ideal.zero_mem _
133	
134	end AlgebraicGeometry

name: horizon
description: How to work inside an Archon Horizon workspace — orient from on-disk state, pick the highest-value formalization work, record progress as commits, and coordinate. Load this first; it points to the specialized skills for detail. Editable per workspace.
---

You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.

## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate

Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.

You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
**shared state**, not meetings:

- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
  another team.
- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).

Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,
`ACTION` unread conversations, advisory unread inbox, then session/runtime and
other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
object in `horizon inbox list --json`.

## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)

**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.

The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):

- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:
  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
- **Inbox attention order** — before edits, inspect all open `protection` items
  (standing constraints, whether read or unread), then open unread
  `conversation` items and reply or mark them read. Other kinds are advisory
  context. In an agent session an unqualified `inbox list` defaults to open items
  and sorts in this order; use an explicit status to audit history.
- **Conversation discipline** — use a conversation only when a reply/decision is
  expected. Search and reuse an open thread before starting one. Its initiator is
  a participant and owns closure: after consuming the answer, add a concise
  conclusion if needed and archive the thread. Reply to human-started threads but
  leave their closure to the human unless asked otherwise (skill: `horizon-inbox`).
- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.

## Your session's identity (environment variables)

The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT` | workspace root (use for `--root`-free CLI calls) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL` | absolute path to this `SKILL.md` (never resolve it relative to the shell cwd) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` | run id (e.g. `0163`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION` | this session's name (e.g. `0002-horizon-T-1`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR` | this session's directory (transcript, usage.json, report) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS` | which round this is (0-based) / the run's planned total |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE` | the task id / title (full body: `"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS` | comma-separated projects this task spans |
| `HORIZON_BIN`, `HORIZON_GIT` | absolute paths to the CLI and the ledger-git wrapper |
| `HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR`, `HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE` | the workspace ledger repo + its work tree — `"$HORIZON_GIT" …` is shorthand for `git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" …` |

## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)

Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:

- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).

## One-shot discipline (important)

This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).

## Pick the highest-value work

Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.

If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
the objective is large. Leave a concise task comment only for a durable state
change or blocker, not every action. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
(it returns to the queue).

## Fresh-context checkpoints

The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
checkpoints:

- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
  clean/build result.

Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
terminal `done` claim.

Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.

## Warnings are work

Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
why.

Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
issue rather than repeated no-op calls.

2	name: project-git
3	description: How git works in an Archon Horizon workspace — one out-of-tree workspace ledger (no per-project repos); read a project's history by pathspec or by a session's commit trailers.
4	---
5	
6	Read this before running `git diff`/`git log` on a project.
7	
8	## The model
9	
10	- **One out-of-tree workspace ledger.** Archon commits to a single repo whose git
11	  dir is `.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git` with the workspace **root** as its
12	  work tree (driven via `--git-dir`/`--work-tree`). `<root>/.git` is deliberately
13	  untouched — it is reserved for a user repo. The ledger records one commit per
14	  completed session: `config.yaml`, the session's scoped project files, and
15	  `.archon-horizon/` shared state; never the binary git dirs under
16	  `.archon-horizon/vcs/`, locks, or other volatile internals.
17	- **There are no per-project repositories.** A project directory has no nested
18	  `.git/`, and there is no `.archon-horizon/vcs/<project>.git`. A project's
19	  "history" is simply the workspace ledger filtered to that project's path.
20	- **You record your own work by committing to the ledger** with plain `git` (see
21	  below). Commit after each independently useful, verified proof/file/tooling
22	  change, before a long build or delegated review, and before expanding scope.
23	  A multi-hour implementation session should normally have several commits; one
24	  commit is appropriate only when the work is genuinely atomic. The message +
25	  diff is how progress is read, so use a semantic, math-first subject. Provenance
26	  trailers are added automatically; do not write them.
27	
28	So a plain `git diff` at the root sees only a user repo (if any), never Archon's.
29	Drive the out-of-tree workspace ledger explicitly (or use `hgit`).
30	
31	## Recording your work (committing)
32	
33	Commits go to the ledger, **not** to `<root>/.git` and **not** via any project
34	`.git` (there is none). Do **not** `export GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE` yourself — that
35	would redirect `lake` and other tooling. Two equivalent ways to commit:
36	
37	```bash
38	# 1) The `hgit` wrapper (on the session env as $HORIZON_GIT) — plain git, ledger-scoped:
39	"$HORIZON_GIT" add path/to/File.lean
40	"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
41	  --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'
42	
43	# 2) The explicit form (identical effect):
44	git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
45	    add path/to/File.lean
46	git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
47	    commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
48	    --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'
49	```
50	
51	Ordinary git: the ledger's index tracks HEAD, so `add` then `commit` records your
52	files on top of it. Horizon's own commits stage in a private index and never leave
53	anything staged in your way.
54	
55	- **Prefer the pathspec commit** — name the paths on the commit itself:
56	  `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…" --trailer 'Summary=…' -- path/to/File.lean`
57	  It records exactly those files, ignores whatever else may be staged, and git
58	  builds its tree from the **current** HEAD — so it cannot silently revert a
59	  concurrent session's files the way a commit built on a stale index can.
60	- Add at least one **`Summary` trailer** explaining the important change, not
61	  merely repeating the subject. Use one trailer per distinct explanation when
62	  useful. Its value supports Markdown and LaTeX, so concise mathematical context
63	  such as `--trailer 'Summary=**Invariant.** Preserves $f(x)=x$ on $A$.'` renders
64	  directly in the dashboard commit item. Keep each trailer on one line; repeat
65	  `--trailer 'Summary=…'` for a few separate points.
66	- Do not wait for the whole task to be complete. A checkpoint commit must build
67	  or otherwise be internally coherent, but it may explicitly leave the next
68	  named obligation open.
69	- Stage **explicit paths** you changed rather than `add -A` — the work tree is the
70	  whole workspace, so `-A` can sweep in unrelated files.
71	- `Archon-Run`/`Session`/`Role`/`Task`/`Projects` trailers are stamped for you by a
72	  hook from the session env; your message stays clean.
73	- Build artifacts (`.lake`, `*.olean`, …) are excluded automatically, and any
74	  high-confidence credential is **redacted to `XXXX`** in the staged content (not
75	  blocked), so a broad add still won't leak a secret into the ledger.
76	- If the guard reports *"redacted possible secret(s) to XXXX"*, it scrubbed a
77	  matched credential and let the commit through — **rotate the real credential**,
78	  and check you didn't stage more than you meant to (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_SECRETS=1`
79	  skips the scan entirely). A *separate* guard still **blocks** a commit that would
80	  silently delete tracked files you didn't change (a stale-index clobber); re-seed
81	  the index (`git read-tree HEAD && git add -- <your files>`) rather than forcing it.
82	
83	Then verify **in the ledger**, and verify the **paths**, not just the SHA — a bare
84	`git cat-file` runs against `<root>/.git`, which has not seen your commit yet and will
85	make a perfectly real SHA look fabricated:
86	
87	```bash
88	"$HORIZON_GIT" ls-tree --name-only HEAD -- path/to/File.lean   # empty ⇒ NOT in HEAD
89	```
90	
91	## Concurrent sessions and the clobber guard
92	
93	Several sessions may commit to the ledger at once. A commit whose index was
94	seeded from an older HEAD (e.g. `read-tree`, then a concurrent session commits,
95	then you commit) produces a tree that *lacks* the other session's new files —
96	plain git would commit it without any error and silently delete their work.
97	The ledger's `pre-commit` guard now rejects any commit that stages deletions
98	you did not ask for:
99	
100	- *"this commit would DELETE N tracked file(s) you did not change"* — your
101	  index base is stale (or you are committing through a polluted shared index).
102	  **Do not override.** Re-seed and retry; your own edits are safe in the
103	  working tree, which concurrent commits never touch:
104	
105	  ```bash
106	  "$HORIZON_GIT" read-tree HEAD
107	  "$HORIZON_GIT" add -- <your files>
108	  "$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…"          # or just: commit -m "…" -- <your files>
109	  ```
110	
111	- Deleting a file **on purpose** (moved/retired): set
112	  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_DELETIONS=1` for that one commit.
113	
114	At the **end of the session**, re-verify content — not just that HEAD moved —
115	since a stale-based commit elsewhere could have landed after yours (the guard
116	blocks new offenders, but belt-and-braces):
117	
118	```bash
119	"$HORIZON_GIT" cat-file -e HEAD:path/to/File.lean && \
120	"$HORIZON_GIT" show HEAD:path/to/File.lean | diff -q - path/to/File.lean
121	```
122	
123	If you were clobbered anyway: `read-tree HEAD`, re-add your files from the
124	working tree, commit once.
125	
126	## Reading history / a project's diff
127	
128	Run from the workspace root:
129	
130	```bash
131	GD=.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git
132	
133	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20                       # whole ledger
134	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20 -- <project-path>     # one project
135	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- <project-path>
136	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- '<project-path>/*.lean'
137	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. show <sha>
138	```
139	
140	Each commit carries provenance trailers — `Archon-Run`, `Archon-Session`,
141	`Archon-Role`, `Archon-Task`, `Archon-Projects` — so you can map a commit to the
142	run/session that made it and see what it touched without parsing prose:
143	
144	```bash
145	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. \
146	  log --format='%H %(trailers:key=Archon-Session,valueonly)' -- <project-path>
147	```
148	
149	To see what the previous Horizon agent changed, find its session's commit(s) by
150	the `Archon-Session` trailer and diff each against **its own parent** (what that
151	commit changed).
152	
153	## Caveats
154	
155	- With parallel runs the ledger is one shared branch: commits from several runs
156	  interleave, and a commit's parent may belong to another run or a dashboard
157	  publish. Diff a commit against its own parent (what *that* commit changed), not
158	  across a span of sessions — that would fold in unrelated runs' changes.
159	- The bundled author identity is `Archon Horizon <archon-horizon@local>`.
